sections.h2: Which county handles a Katy house?
sections.html:
West of Houston, Katy straddles three counties: Fort Bend, Harris and Waller. Your parcel decides which county appraises and taxes the house, and your tax statement names it.

The city covers 15.35 square miles and estimates its 2025 population at 28,121, up from about 8,000 in 1990. Growth has meant steady demand for houses, along with plenty of newer competing listings. Fort Bend Central Appraisal District offers a parcel search and online map for confirming a property. A parcel in Harris or Waller County belongs to that county's own appraisal district and tax office.

sections.h2: Older downtown Katy and newer subdivisions
sections.html:
The town site was platted in 1895 along the railroad and rebuilt after the 1900 hurricane. Katy became a city in 1945, and a local committee placed historical markers on more than a dozen older homes and buildings downtown in 1986. Much newer housing now surrounds that core.

Own one of the older downtown houses? Check with city planning staff on what rules apply before ordering exterior work. Period details deserve a line in your pitch, and the markers make a pleasant walking tour for out-of-town buyers.

sections.h2: Which repairs need a city permit?
sections.html:
For most structural, mechanical and outdoor jobs, yes. Katy's Permit and Building Services division wants a permit for new construction, remodeling, roofing, heating and cooling systems, electrical and plumbing, and anything that adds or removes walls.

Pools, hot tubs, storage buildings, carports, garages, driveways, sidewalks, patios, irrigation, water heaters, demolition and house moving are on the list too. An online portal handles applications, plan uploads, payments and inspection scheduling. Card payments add a convenience fee of 3.95 percent or $3.00, whichever is greater.

Inspections often snag on work done without a permit. Say a previous owner finished a garage or added a patio on the quiet: a buyer with a loan may balk, and an investor paying cash will simply discount the price.

sections.h2: Texas tax dates around a Katy closing
sections.html:
Katy bills carry a lien dated January 1 and arrive in early October. Your closing day therefore decides who carries which slice of the year.

The Katy tax year at a glance
DateWhat happens
January 1Appraisals reflect value and ownership as of this day
May 15Usual protest cutoff, or 30 days after a late notice
Around October 1Bills are mailed
February 1Most unpaid balances turn delinquent

A homestead appraisal can climb only ten percent in a year. Fort Bend CAD takes homestead filings online and accepts appeals by mail, in person or online.

sections.h2: Options if you need to sell fast in Katy
sections.html:
Your calendar and repair budget will usually choose among three routes.

  • Listing: the widest audience, at the price of open houses, a repair list and weeks of waiting.
  • Selling alone: you keep the commission and take on the contract and the marketing.
  • Cash: with no lender appraisal, the buyer can accept the property unrepaired and close on your date.

Deferred maintenance, sitting renters or an unsettled estate all point toward cash, which erases the repair list. Compare any offer with what a listing would truly net after commission and repairs.

A Katy deed is filed with the clerk of whichever county holds the parcel: Fort Bend, Harris or Waller. A notary has to witness your signature first, and the price is per page plus records charges. The title company normally records it, so look for the final amount on your settlement statement. Keep a recorded copy afterward. If a tax bill from the year of sale arrives later, that copy and your settlement statement show who owed which share of the year.

sections.h2: If your Katy house is headed for a tax auction
sections.html:
Taxes left unpaid long enough let the taxing unit sue, and the house may go to a tax foreclosure auction run by the constable or an agent the unit hires. No single statewide list of auctions exists, so watch the county clerk and tax office sites for Fort Bend, Harris or Waller.

An owner can still buy the property back in some cases. For a homestead, farm or mineral interest there is a two-year window from the date the buyer's deed is filed, with a 25 percent premium in the first year and 50 percent in the second, plus the bid, recording fee, taxes, penalties and costs. Other property gets 180 days at a premium of up to 25 percent. Money left over after the sale belongs to the former owner, who has two years from the sale to claim it.

If you owe back taxes, a sale before any suit usually costs far less than letting it reach auction, since court costs and attorney fees are added along the way.

sections.h2: A mortgage in default or an inherited house
sections.html:
A Katy loan in default moves along the Texas out-of-court track: a default letter, a brief chance to catch up, then a posted and recorded sale notice and an auction on a first Tuesday. A housing counselor can show where your loan stands.

Inheriting from a relative? Find out whether a will exists and whether anyone opened probate. To keep the homestead tax break, heirs show the appraisal district proof of kinship and the death certificate. A lawyer in Harris, Fort Bend or Waller County can name the right deed route.

sections.h2: Papers and disclosures for a smooth Katy sale
sections.html: Bring together the deed, any payoff letter, the newest tax statement from the right county and records of permits for past work. A loan-backed buyer will probably ask for repairs after inspection, while a cash buyer takes the property as is and prices the risk. Settling these points early keeps a Katy contract moving.

sections.h2: How the sale timeline works in Katy
sections.html:
Listing a Katy house begins with showings and an offer, followed by inspection and repair talks. A financed buyer adds an appraisal, and the title company searches before signing, so plan for several weeks. A cash buyer can skip the appraisal and accept the house unrepaired, shortening the road.

On any route, get a closing date in writing along with a plain division of title and recording charges. If renters live there, line the date up with the end of their lease. Since Katy parcels sit in three counties, find out early which clerk files your deed and which tax office issues the payoff statement.

Earlier additions cause more friction than almost anything else in a Katy sale. A garage, a patio or a replaced heating and cooling system may have gone in with no permit on file. Ask city staff whether any record exists. If none does, tell the buyer in writing before the inspector turns it up. A loan buyer may want the work permitted first, which takes time, while a cash buyer typically adjusts the price. Raising it yourself makes either outcome easier.

faqs.q: Is Katy in Harris County or Fort Bend County?
faqs.a: Both, and Waller County as well. The county on your tax statement tells you which appraisal district and tax office apply to your house.

faqs.q: Is a roofing permit needed in Katy?
faqs.a: Yes. Roofing sits on the city's permit list with remodeling and heating and cooling replacement. Use the online portal to apply.
The city estimates 28,121 for 2025, up from 21,894 in 2020.

faqs.q: By what date must a Katy owner protest the appraisal?
faqs.a: The usual cutoff is May 15, or 30 days from delivery if the notice arrived late. File with the appraisal district for the county where your parcel lies.

faqs.q: Will anyone buy a Katy house with unfinished repairs?
faqs.a: Yes, if the buyer takes it as is. A buyer with a loan will likely want repairs after inspection, so disclose unpermitted work early.
